title: QuarterSumLadder: a Lean 4 formalization of the quarter-sum ladder and the weight-two congruences
description:
Lean 4 / Mathlib formalization accompanying J. S. Farland, "The quarter-sum ladder and the weight-two congruences, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23797239). Let p = 1 (mod 8) be prime and chi a quartic character modulo p, so that chi is even and w = chi(2) = +-1. Put Q = (p - 1)/4, let R_r count the 0 < n < p/4 with chi(n) = i^r, and let Omega = x + iy be the quarter sum of chi over (0, p/4), whose norm is half the relative class number of the imaginary cyclic quartic field of conductor 4p (quoted, not formalized). The development proves that the coordinates of B_{2,chi} = c_0 + i c_1 are integers divisible by 4, with residues modulo 8 given by counts of integers m = 2 (mod 4) in the classes of chi, and that both are divisible by 8 exactly when 2 is a fourth power modulo p. A single product argument of Gauss and Lehmer gives the quartic Gauss lemma w = (-1)^(R_1 + R_3), the parity of the four quarter counts when w = 1, and the parity of R_2 through the order of 2. From these it proves criteria in terms of the quarter counts for 2^k | 2N(Omega) with 2 <= k <= 6, the formula v_2(x^2 + y^2) = 2 min(v_2 x, v_2 y) + [v_2 x = v_2 y], the congruence p(c_0 - c_1) = -4(x - y) (mod 16), and the valuation of B_{2,chi} at 1 + i, which is 5, 6, or at least 7.

The statements are in Challenge.lean. Lean's comparator checks them against the proofs, with the definition bodies compared, and the proofs are replayed in the Lean, nanoda and con-ron kernels. No sorry, no native_decide; standard axioms only. The changes in each version are described in the release notes on GitHub: github.com/jkfarland-bot/Quartersumladder/releases.
notes: AI assistance: the Lean code in this record was drafted and repaired by Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, from the statements and proofs of the companion paper "The quarter-sum ladder and the weight-two congruences, formalized in Lean" (doi:10.5281/zenodo.23797239), and compiled locally with lake. Every proof is checked by the Lean kernel, and Comparator replays the solution against the statement file under the Lean, NanoDa and con-ron kernels. The author, Joseph S. Farland, chose the scope, directed the work, and is responsible for the contents. No external human reviewer has checked the formalization.
